title: Introduce throughput window harmonizer and variance buffering provisioner
author: Marcus Li
description:
Motivation: We observed frequent short-lived microbursts from several tenants that cause the autoscaler to oscillate between provisioning and decommitting capacity. Current smoothing layers operate on fixed windows which either over-smooth (masking real sustained load) or under-smooth (reacting to noise). This PR introduces two complementary components: a throughput-window-harmonizer (a dynamic, seqlen-aware window estimator) and a variance-buffering provisioner (fractional reserve token reservoir with randomized decay).

Design summary: The throughput-window-harmonizer maintains an adaptive window per tenant/model that expands or contracts based on a variance-weighted EWMA of recent throughput samples; it uses median-filtering to reject outlier spikes and applies sequence-length (seqlen) weighting so requests that produce longer KV-cache lifetimes have higher influence. The harmonizer exposes a stable target throughput percentile (configurable, default p95) that downstream allocators use instead of raw instantaneous RPS. The variance-buffering provisioner consumes the harmonized signal and maintains a small fractional reserve (buffer tokens) sized by recent variance and a conservative growth factor; tokens are decayed using a randomized half-life to avoid synchronized decommit waves across tenants. The provisioner also supports a soft-grace admission path where requests may draw burst credits when available, with telemetry hooks to record borrow/repay events.

Backward compatibility and rollout: Both features are gated behind a runtime feature flag (harmonizer_v1) and default off for all tenants. The autoscaler has a backward-compatible fallback to the existing windowing when the flag is disabled. Config knobs are exposed via dedicated-configs and documented in the console: harmonizer.enabled, harmonizer.target_percentile, provisioner.buffer_min, provisioner.decay_half_life_ms.

Telemetry and observability: Added new metrics: redwood.provisioner.buffer_size, redwood.provisioner.borrow_count, redwood.harmonizer.window_ms_p50/p90/p95, redwood.harmonizer.seqlen_weight_total, redwood.tenant.headroom_delta. Instrumented traces for "harmonizer.evaluate" and "provisioner.borrow" (span tags: tenant, model, seqlen). Console dashboards: proactive panel showing tenant buffer usage and a regression alert when borrow_count/pod_count ratio exceeds threshold.

Testing: Unit tests for EWMA/median filtering and seqlen-weighting. Integration harness simulates 100 tenants with randomized microbursts and long-tail sustained loads; assertion checks ensure no more than 8% extra capacity churn compared to baseline under synthetic microburst traffic. Added flaky-tolerant integration test that was rerun in CI once.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of harmonizer and provisioner core logic
- [x] Telemetry + traces
- [x] Config and feature-flag gating
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Console panels and release notes entry

Commits summary: the series implements the harmonizer algorithm, the buffer reservoir with randomized decay, integration with the autoscaler decision path, telemetry, and tests. See commits below for granular changes.

Changed areas (high-level): runtime/autoscaler (decision path), runtime/autoscaler/harmonizer (new package), runtime/autoscaler/provisioner (new package), infra/metrics (added metric definitions), console/dashboards (new panel), tests/integration (microburst harness).

Risk notes: The provisioner intentionally keeps conservative defaults (buffer_min=0.05 of committed capacity) to limit over-provisioning risk. Memory overhead: harmonizer maintains small sliding windows (per-tenant ring buffers); stress profiling shows ~2.5KB per active tenant in worst case. Feature is gated and can be disabled if issues appear after rollout.

Related: ENG-2345 (adaptive smoothing initiative), ENG-2401 (autoscaler stability spikes), SUP-987 (customer report of oscillation on dedicated pools).

review_comments: Sofia Patel: Can we bound memory usage in high-tenant-count clusters? Please add a defensive cap on per-tenant ring buffer and document the worst-case overhead.
Marcus Li (author): Added cap of 256 samples per tenant with evict oldest behavior; added memory estimate comments in harmonizer.go and profiler output to the PR description.
Priya Nandan: Edge-case on cold start: harmonizer may output a near-zero target and cause slow ramp. Please ensure the provisioner seeds a minimal buffer for cold tenants.
Marcus Li (author): Provisioner now seeds buffer_min on first evaluation and records a metric redwood.provisioner.seeded=true for auditability.
release_notes: Add a gated throughput-window harmonizer to produce stable per-tenant throughput targets and a variance-buffering provisioner that holds fractional burst credits. Defaults are conservative and feature is off by default; opt-in recommended for experimental dedicated pools to reduce capacity oscillation during microbursts.
